conviction_note: Q2's guidance arithmetic (NIM above 4.15%, opex about $48.5m, loan growth on the $1bn track) gives a pre-provision run-rate of about $2.50-2.60, slightly above a disputed $2.38-2.48 bar. The board raised the dividend again the day before the print, knowing the Q3 numbers. Against that, two of the last four quarters were wrecked by idiosyncratic credit hits, and NYC rent-stabilised multifamily faces a 0% two-year freeze from Oct 1. The positive findings net to only +0.2. Because the bar is disputed, p_up is held at 54 on a 6% absolute move (between the 7.86% indicative straddle, whose spread is 55% of mid, and the 4.84% historical median), which gives +0.48.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS: $2.38 at MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MCB/earnings/, read 2026-10-20) against $2.48 at Tickflow (range $2.46-2.49 from 2 analysts, revenue about $97M; https://www.tickflow.io/stock/MCB/forecast, search snippet only, page returned 429). The two sources disagree by $0.10, so the bar is treated as disputed and every finding is capped small. The company gives no EPS guide. Its Q2 call guided Q3 NIM 'north of' 4.15%, opex run-rate about $48.5M a quarter, full-year NII growth of at least 20%, $1bn of 2026 loan growth and $7.5-10M of recoveries by year-end (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2940590).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-19, the day before the print, the board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.40, up from $0.35. That is the second raise in two quarters ($0.25 to $0.35 in July to $0.40) and was declared with the board already holding the Q3 numbers. The market's bar implies a clean, provision-light quarter; a board that had just booked another large credit hit would be unlikely to raise the payout 14% the day before reporting it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July raise ($0.25 to $0.35) was declared 2026-07-20, the day before Q2, and the stock still fell 8.96% on Q2's credit-driven miss. So a pre-print dividend raise has not protected this name from a credit surprise; it is a weak signal, not a guarantee.
findings.why_not_priced: It went public one session before the print in an 8-K exhibit, not a headline release. Part of the +2.18% five-day run-up may already reflect it. If it were fully read as 'Q3 is clean', the stock would be closer to the $92 it held in August, and the straddle would not still be pricing a 7.9% event move.
findings.independence: The CFO's open-market purchase of 1,000 shares at $89.98 on 2026-07-23 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1476034/000200027626000006/xslF345X06/form4-07272026_060701.xml) points the same way from a different document, though it is weak and offset by director sales (see the insider finding).

findings.finding: The company's own Q3 guidance adds up to EPS of about $2.50-2.60 before any unusual provision, against a bar of $2.38 (MarketBeat) to $2.48 (Tickflow). The inputs: Q2 NII of $90.4M at a 4.08% NIM, Q3 NIM guided above 4.15% on about $8.9bn of earning assets (about $93-94M NII), $2.6M of fee income, $48.5M opex, a roughly $2-4M growth provision, a 29-30% tax rate and about 12.4M shares. The 7.6% year-to-date loan growth and the $1bn pipeline support the balance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Clean quarters have been rewarded: Q4 2025 (2026-01-20) rose 13.91% and Q1 2025 (2025-01-23) rose 7.89%. Q2 2026 had NII up 22.8% year on year and NIM in line, and still fell 8.96% because of the provision. Core PPNR has not been the line the stock trades on when credit is noisy.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: this lands inside what the company guided, and the higher $2.48 estimate is essentially the same arithmetic. The open part is the $0.10 gap between the two estimate sources. If the street had converged on the guide math, both aggregators would read about $2.50.
findings.independence: Base figures come from the company's Q2 release (https://s206.q4cdn.com/586823346/files/doc_news/Metropolitan-Bank-Holding-Corp--Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf). The guidance is corroborated by a second call summary (https://quartr.com/events/metropolitan-bank-holding-corp-mcb-q2-2026_oneYZa10), which says the same thing; both are readings of one call.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CEO said he expects $7.5-10M of recoveries 'between now and the end of the year'. He also said a Kansas City credit carried at $22M (a $24M loan less a $2M specific reserve) had settled for $27M, with a 'significant principal paydown by year-end'. Any part landing in Q3 lowers the provision: each $5M is about $0.28 of EPS after tax on 12.4M shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The Q1 2026 EPS of $2.92 was flattered by an allowance methodology change that cut the ACL, and the stock fell 1.37% on that print, so this name has not paid much for provision tailwinds.
findings.why_not_priced: The recoveries were explicitly 'without giving specific guidance' and their timing is unstated, so estimates likely carry a normal provision. If they were in the bar, the $2.48 estimate would sit nearer $2.70-2.90. It is partly a one-off below PPNR, so sized as a fraction of the same money as core earnings.
findings.independence: Same call transcript as the guidance-arithmetic finding (one document). The Quartr summary (https://quartr.com/events/metropolitan-bank-holding-corp-mcb-q2-2026_oneYZa10) repeats the $7.5-10M figure.

findings.finding: Credit is this name's recurring failure line. Q3 2025 printed $0.67 against about $1.95 consensus and Q2 2026 printed $1.54 against $2.30, both on idiosyncratic provisions. After the Q1 2026 methodology change and the Q2 charge-offs, the ACL is down to $62.0M, 0.85% of $7.33bn of loans. Named problem credits remain: a $16M window-and-door C&I term loan on nonaccrual, a $14M restructured out-of-market multifamily loan and a high-net-worth relationship with a rejected $2M offer. Any of these, or a new one, can erase a quarter's beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit-hit quarters: 2025-10-23 fell 4.84% (EPS $0.67) and 2026-07-21 fell 8.96% (EPS $1.54). Two of the last four prints, and the two largest negative reactions in the seven-print history.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as a tail: the stock trades 13% off its high and well below KBW's cut $110 target (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MCB/sentiment). The residual is the thin 0.85% reserve after methodology changes, which gives little cushion for another specific reserve. A market that had fully priced a third hit would trade nearer the $85 offering price, with consensus well below the guide arithmetic.
findings.independence: The problem-credit detail comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2940590), a different document from the release. The Q3 2025 miss is from Zacks via Finviz (https://finviz.com/news/203219/metropolitan-bank-holding-corp-mcb-misses-q3-earnings-estimates).

findings.finding: NYC's Rent Guidelines Board voted 7-1 on 2026-06-25 for a 0% increase on both one- and two-year rent-stabilised leases, effective for leases from 2026-10-01, the first multi-year freeze in its history. A NYC peer, ConnectOne, had already taken a $13.8M charge-off on rent-stabilised multifamily in Q2 2026. MCB is a NYC CRE lender with a legacy multifamily workout. Its rent-regulated share could not be sourced, and its CRE book is mostly not legacy rent-stabilised thrift lending.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No MCB print has turned on rent-regulated multifamily specifically. The Q2 2026 out-of-market multifamily charge-off was already reserved and was not the driver of that quarter's fall.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public since June. What remains is that Q3 is the first quarter in which banks may re-grade rent-stabilised loans for a two-year 0% path. A market pricing it as an MCB-specific problem would show MCB underperforming NYC peers since June, and this was not checked.
findings.independence: The ConnectOne Q2 2026 charge-off (https://247wallst.com/cards/connectone-bancorp-inc-q2-2026-earnings-cnob-01ky7c0wefk82njyth7zyrtbqm) is a different source. This is a proxy: MCB has not quantified its own rent-regulated exposure in anything found.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the fed funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, 12-0. MCB's Q2 NIM path (above 4.15% in Q3, pressing toward 4.20% in Q4) assumed no change in the target. Non-interest-bearing deposits are 20.6% of deposits (10-Q, June 30) and new loan coupons are 'well above 7%', so a hike more likely lifts the Q4 NIM outlook than cuts it. The Q3 effect is about two weeks, and the 10-Q's rate-sensitivity table was not read, so the sign is inference.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (2026-01-20) rose 13.91% on a print that carried the forward outlook. No direct precedent of a rate move changing MCB's NIM guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is fully public. What is not public is whether MCB updates its Q4 NIM target above 4.20% on the call (2026-10-21, inside the window). If the market expected a raised NIM path, consensus would sit above the guide arithmetic rather than at or below it.
findings.independence: The 20.6% NIB share is from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1476034/000110465926089011/mcb-20260630x10q.htm). This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed, so it is a proxy.

findings.finding: Insider trading since the Q2 print is mixed and small. The CFO bought 1,000 shares at $89.98 on 2026-07-23. Director Robert Patent sold 10,000 at $92.29 on 2026-08-10 (76,185 left), and director Dale Fredston sold 2,000 at $89.09 on 2026-09-17, about two weeks before quarter-end (14,668 left).
findings.why_not_priced: These are small Form 4s on EDGAR. Twelve thousand shares sold against one thousand bought is too little to read as a view; if it carried information, the sales would be clustered and from officers.
findings.independence: The other two filings are separate Form 4s: Patent (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1008343/000100834326000007/xslF345X06/form4-08122026_050801.xml) and Dougherty (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1476034/000200027626000006/xslF345X06/form4-07272026_060701.xml).

findings.finding: A new $50M repurchase program was approved 2026-06-19, about 4.5% of a roughly $1.09bn market cap. The 10-Q shows no repurchases in Q2 (123,061 shares, all in Q1, for $9.9M) and 12,397,778 shares outstanding on 2026-07-27. Whether MCB bought in Q3, with the stock at $88-92 near the $85 offering price, is disclosed only in tonight's release.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public. Its Q3 use is not. Even a full $50M would move EPS by only about 1-2% in the quarter, so it is small either way.
findings.independence: The Q2 release reports the authorisation (https://s206.q4cdn.com/586823346/files/doc_news/Metropolitan-Bank-Holding-Corp--Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf). It shares the company-capital-return theme with the dividend finding but rests on a different fact.

baseline_tension: The baseline makes no directional statement (skew null, chain illiquid), and the run-up is flat over 20 days and +2.2% over 5 days, so a mild positive lean from guidance, dividend and recoveries cuts against nothing. The real tension is with the name's own history: two of the last four prints were sold hard on credit.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, bar disputed ($2.38 MarketBeat against $2.48 Tickflow): guidance arithmetic 0.7 to 0.4 and recoveries 0.5 to 0.3, capped small; p_up 56 to 54; print_vs_bar 3.0 to 2.0
Rule 6, inside guidance: the guidance-arithmetic finding lands inside the company's Q3 NIM/opex guide, so it was moved toward 0 (same cut as above, applied once)
Rule 1, verified fact is not a reaction: dividend raise 0.8 to 0.6, since a pre-print raise in July did not stop a -8.96% reaction
Rule 5, proxy: rent freeze -0.4 to -0.3 and Fed hike 0.3 to 0.2, both macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed; kept as filed
Rule 7: short interest checked before the negatives (about 4.5% of shares out, 3.2 days, stale March 2026), not crowded, so the credit negative was not shrunk for squeeze risk
Credit base-rate (-1.0), insiders (-0.1) and buyback (+0.1) left unchanged
